replace.why: Real MotorInclude.h lines 72..75 are four `extern interrupt void ..._isr(void);` prototypes; `interrupt` is a C28x keyword and MSVC reports C2054. Dropping the keyword leaves plain void(void) prototypes: no function name or parameter changes, and the patch is host-only, so the target build is unaffected.

Real DSP2803x_PieVect.h line 9. MotorPWM does not touch PieVectTable, but the case shim's DSP2803x_Device.h includes this header exactly as the real device header does, so it must parse. Only the keyword is removed; the struct layout is untouched.

MotorPWM.c line 2 includes MotorPwmInclude.h and this header's line 10 includes MotorInclude.h. Left quoted, MSVC resolves it from include/motor/ (the same directory as MotorPwmInclude.h itself) and gets the UNPATCHED MotorInclude.h with the four `extern interrupt void` prototypes -- the gen_dir copy would never be reached, C2054. Angle brackets drop the same-directory rule, gen_dir is first on the include path, so the patched copy wins. Same trap MotorSVC hit through MotorVCInclude.h.

Reached from the patched MotorInclude.h (line 12). That copy lives in gen_dir, so its quoted includes already resolve to gen_dir first -- this entry is kept for symmetry with the MotorSVC case and to make the dependency explicit: if the include order inside MotorInclude.h ever changes so MotorVCInclude.h is reached from include/motor/ instead, the unpatched quoted include would reappear here first.

`extern int absl(long int);` (line 76) and `extern int qatan(long int);` (line 78). The case shim ends with `#define int short`, so `long int` expands to `long short` and MSVC rejects it (C2632). `long` and `long int` are the same type, so the width is unchanged. Neither function is called by MotorPWM, but both must parse.
